scope: Source review after the closed library sample and native viability failure; hypotheses are untested.

reviewed.finding: Integer leaves that fit i64 use Rational::new; larger integers use the original BigInt conversion.

Canonical small integers cover magnitudes 2 through 64 plus the separate zero/one paths. Wider primitive integers construct BigUint from u128. The BigInt path transfers the cloned magnitude and skips GCD when its denominator is one.
The canonical positive and negative tables each contain 63 OnceLock slots.
The new tri-state helper retains the same lazy x-then-y coordinate zero tests, while public PartialEq is unchanged.
Approximate/preview queries still enter tri-state comparison before repeating original policy equality; certified negative reuse applies only to exact non-preview policies.

A closed certificate copies rational/radical payloads on publication and retrieval. Shared-node local memo copies remain. The first retained pass may retry the original recognizer only after failure with reuse, after dropping its first memo.
Retained payload is reconstructed under a read lock; publication first creates a closed copy, then writes only an empty field.
Existing public tracing can count rational temporaries, reductions, GCDs and dispatch labels in explicit scopes without changing runtime source.
Linux PerformanceTimer uses CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID for the worker test thread; this is not whole-process wall time.

dependency.finding: Primitive u64/u128 construction pushes digits into an initially empty Vec; BigUint::clone clones its existing digit slice. This is a plausible allocation mechanism, not a measured attribution of the signed-word row.

unimplemented_hypotheses: Limit integer-leaf canonical reuse to existing cached values while preserving the original wider-value conversion, with the table boundary owned by Rational.

Route approximate/preview endpoint handling through the original boolean sequence before entering tri-state negative-proof reuse. Existing attribution does not prove the retained payload responsible for its three extra allocations.
Measure existing rational/dispatch counts in cache-bearing and cache-free construction/query phases to distinguish extra arithmetic from certificate handling before proposing another cache change.
constraints: The cache-free combination failed the native board gate; small consumer tweaks have no demonstrated ability to close that gap.
Do not remove the mandatory cache-free retry or weaken retained-fact semantics.
Existing rejected storage, projection, memo and coefficient variants remain closed.
No new runtime prototype or causal timing claim follows from this review alone.
